sentences.text: The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.91,163/ for the damage caused to the Electricity Spun Pole in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.3506/2021 24.01.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA41B2043 being driven by the 3rd respondent in a rash and negligent manner and while taking UTurn in a reverse direction he dashed against 11 mtr. long spun pole erected on the footpath at MEI Road, Opposite Hyundai Services Center, Bangalore and thereby caused loss to the BESCOM.
The Respondent No.2 is the owner of said lorry and in this regard FIR came to be registered in Crime No.13/2020 at Yeshwanthapura traffic police station.
3. Further the petitioner has stated that he spent sum of Rs.91,163/ including labour charges in order to replace the said electrical pole.
Hence, Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending lorry and Respondent No.2 being the owner of the lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, he has prayed to award compensation of Rs.91,163/ from the respondents.
4. The summons has been duly served on SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.3506/2021 have not appeared before this Tribunal.
Hence, respondent No.2 and 3 have been placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 has appeared before this tribunal through his counsel and filed written statement.
The Respondent No.3 has contended that the owner of the offending lorry and the police have not complied with the provisions of IMV Act after the accident.
Further he has contended that he has issued policy in favour of Respondent No.2 with respect to lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B2043 as such, his liability is subject to terms and conditions fo the policy.
Further he has contended that the Respondent No.3 the driver of the offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

He has also contended that the Respondent No.2 knowingly entrusted his lorry to the Bangalore Electricity Supply Company vs The Royal Sundram General on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83850568/
2 person who was not having valid and effective driving licence as such, he committed breach of terms of policy.

sentences.text: Further he has denied the entire averments of petition as false and baseless.
Hence, SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.3506/2021 he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the the following issues have been framed:
:: ISSUES::
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 24.01.2020 at about 08.00 p.m. respondent No.3 was driving lorry bearing No.KA41B2043 which belongs to respondent No.2 and while taking Uturn at MEI junction, he took reverse turn in rash and negligent manner and dashed against 11 mts long spun pole erected on the footpath, as a result the same was damaged and thereby caused loss to the BESCOM, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
The Assistant Executive Engineer of petitioner company in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW1 and got marked 8 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.8.
His witness an Assistant Engineer (Ele), BESCOM has examined as PW.2 and got 3 documents as Ex.P.9 to P.11.

On the other hand,
the respondents have not chosen to lead any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both sides.
SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.3506/2021 Perused the entire records.

8. My findings to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 REASONS  ISSUE No.1:
 9.
In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW1.
He has got marked 8 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.8.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination in chief.

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the alleged accident and also denied the damage sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove the alleged accident and also the damage sustained by him.

PW.1 in his evidence has stated that on 24.01.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., lorry SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.3506/2021 bearing Reg.No.KA41B2043 being driven by the 3rd respondent in rash and negligent manner and while taking UTurn in a reverse direction he dashed against 11 mtr. long spun pole erected on the footpath at MEI Road, Opposite Hyundai Services Center, Bangalore and thereby caused loss to the BESCOM.
Further he has deposed that in this regard FIR came to be registered in Crime No.13/2020 at Yeshwanthapura traffic police station.
He has also deposed that the BESCOM company has spent sum of Rs.91,163/ towards replacement of new 11 mtr long spun electrical pole.

PW.2 has also filed his affidavit supporting the version of PW.1.
11.

PW.1 and PW.2 in support of their version, they have produced their ID cards, estimation of damage, true copy of complaint, FIR, spot mahazar, charge sheet, rough sketch, certified copy of IMV report, indemnity bond and true copy of notice.

On perusal of Ex.P.3 to 7 it is clear that the accident took place on 24.01.2020 at about 8.30 SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.3506/2021 p.m. but the FIR in this regard came to be registered in crime No.13/2020 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 427 of IPC on 25.01.2020 at Yeshwanthapura traffic police station.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA41B2043 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 427 of IPC.
12.
As per Ex.P.10 - IMV report it appears that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the lorry.
Ex.P.2 shows that, the Petitioner company has already replaced the 11 mtr long spun electrical pole by incurring sum of Rs.91,163/.
The learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 has cross examined PW.1 and 2.
PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that in order to out source one pole it costs around Rs.16,850/.
This means the cost of one pole is Rs.16,850/.

As already stated supra as per Ex.P.2 the Petitioner company has already replaced the 11 mtr long spun electrical SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.3506/2021 pole by incurring sum Rs.91,163/ which includes labour charges, special locality allowance on labour charges, break down charges at 25% on labour for speedy restoration of power, additional labour charges at 10% for working on hazardous installations, service tax at 18% on total labour charges, contribution towards employees provident fund, transportation cost, contingencies and employees costs.
Therefore, though the learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 has cross examined PW.1 and 2 but he has not elicited anything from them to disbelieve their version
. Therefore, there is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police against the Respondent No.3 i.e., the driver of the offending lorry is defective or collusive.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the offending lorry which belongs to the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.3506/2021  ISSUE NO.2 :

sentences.text: DAMAGES:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.2 to show that he has already replaced 11mts long spun pole by incurring sum of Rs.91,163/ due to loss caused by the Respondent No.2 and 3.
The learned counsel for Respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from PW.1 and 2 to disbelieve the contents of Ex.P.2.
Hence, I am of the opinion the Petitioner is entitled to the compensation of Rs.91,163/ under the head loss of damage.

14. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

15. LIABILITY: The respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending lorry and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
The SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.3506/2021 primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

16. ISSUE NO.3 : For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following : : ORDER : The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.91,163/ (Rupees Ninety One Thousand One hundred and Sixty Three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
The entire compensation amount shall be released to the petitioner through E payment on proper identification and verification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.3506/2021
Draw an award accordingly.
